cards.text: We're in the land of Moab, and the LORD has commanded Moses, Israel's leader, to make a covenant with the Israelites. This one comes in addition to the covenant He already made with them at Horeb. Pull up a stool, friend, because this is a BIG one.

cards.question: Moses summons all Israel. What does he start by saying they saw with their own eyes?

answers.text: Everything the LORD did in Egypt
The walls of Jericho falling down
The tower of Babel going up

cards.text: The great trials, the miraculous signs and wonders: they saw ALL of it with their own eyes. Front row seats, friend.

cards.question: But Moses says that to this day, the LORD has not given them a ___ to understand.

cards.text: Seeing every wonder without understanding is me watching the same cookie demo TEN times and STILL burning the batch. Then Moses speaks the LORD's own words: for forty years, He led them through the wilderness.

cards.question: In forty years in the wilderness, Israel's clothes and sandals wore out.

cards.text: Forty years, same sandals, and I can't get one apron through a single holiday rush. They also ate no bread and drank no wine or strong drink that whole time.

cards.question: No bread, no wine and no strong drink in the wilderness. Why does the LORD say it was that way?

answers.text: So they might know He is the LORD their God
So they would be strong enough for battle
So they would long for the promised land

cards.text: Then Moses talks about right here. When they reached this place, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to fight them.

cards.question: Sihon and Og come out against Israel in battle. How does it end?

answers.text: Israel makes peace with both kings

cards.question: Israel takes Sihon and Og's land. Who gets it as an inheritance?

answers.text: Two and a half of the tribes

cards.text: That's the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. Then Moses brings the whole history lesson down to one point: keep and follow the words of this covenant.

cards.question: Moses tells Israel to keep and follow the words of this covenant. Why?

answers.text: So they may prosper in all they do
So their enemies will fear their name
So the nations will follow their God

cards.text: Now Moses looks out at the crowd standing before the LORD today. Leaders of tribes, elders, officials, all the men of Israel, their children and wives: EVERYBODY is here.

cards.question: The foreigners in Israel's camps who cut wood and draw water are left out of this gathering.

cards.text: Even the wood cutters and water carriers made the list, and the expired coupon I shared my old junk drawer with would've been FIRST in line for an invite like that. They're all standing there to enter into the covenant of the LORD their God and into His oath, which He's making with them today.

cards.question: Through this covenant, the LORD will establish them today as His ___

cards.text: And He'll be their God, just as He swore to their fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Then Moses says he's making this covenant and this oath not only with them.

cards.question: Besides the people standing there today, who else is Moses making this covenant with?

answers.text: Those who are not here today
The people of the land of Moab

cards.text: Moses takes them back one more time: they know how they lived in Egypt and how they passed through the nations on the way here.

cards.question: Among those nations, Israel saw idols made of wood and stone, and of silver and gold.

cards.text: So Moses gives a warning: make sure no man or woman, clan or tribe among them has a heart that turns away from the LORD to worship those nations' gods.

cards.question: Moses says to make sure there's no root among them that bears such poisonous and bitter ___

cards.text: That kind of person hears the words of this oath and blesses himself anyway: "I will have peace, even though I walk in the stubbornness of my own heart." Friend, that's me ignoring the oven timer and telling myself the batch is FINE.
But Moses says the LORD will never be willing to forgive him. His anger and jealousy will burn against that man, and every curse written in this book will fall on him.

cards.question: What does Moses say the LORD will do to that man's name?

answers.text: Blot it out from under heaven
Write it in the Book of the Law
Carve it on a stone tablet

cards.text: He'll be singled out from all the tribes of Israel for disaster. Then Moses looks ahead: the generation to come and the foreigner from a distant land will see the plagues and sicknesses the LORD has inflicted on the land.

cards.question: What does Moses say the land's soil will become?

answers.text: A burning waste of sulfur and salt
A muddy swamp full of reeds

cards.question: Moses compares the ruined land to the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah.

cards.text: And all the nations will ask, "Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land? Why this great outburst of anger?"

cards.question: When the nations ask why, what will the people answer?

cards.text: That's the covenant the LORD made with them when He brought them out of Egypt. And they went and served other gods and worshiped them.

cards.question: In that answer, the other gods they worshiped were gods the LORD had given to them.

cards.text: The answer goes on: the anger of the LORD burned against that land. He brought on it every curse written in this book.

cards.question: Then what does the answer say the LORD did with the people?

answers.text: Uprooted them and cast them into another land
Left them in the land to serve their enemies
Sent them back across the Jordan River

cards.text: Moses ends with this: the secret things belong to the LORD our God. Friend, I'm good with that, because I never even figured out which door the mystery key in my old junk drawer opened.

cards.question: The secret things belong to the LORD. Who does Moses say the things revealed belong to?
The things revealed are theirs so that they may ___ all the words of this law.

cards.text: We'll let the ovens rest right here, friend, but Moses is NOT done preaching yet.

findings.problem: The story card ends with "EVERYBODY is here." That gives away card 15, which asks whether the foreigners who cut wood and draw water are left out of the gathering. A baker who just read "EVERYBODY is here" knows the answer is False.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card opens by telling the wood cutters and water carriers from Deuteronomy 29:11, but it cites only Deuteronomy 29:12. It should cite Deuteronomy 29:11-12.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The expired coupon joke only works if the baker knows the coupon "still believed in itself." The line doesn't say that, so a stranger would say "huh?" The joke also sets the foreign workers next to an expired coupon, which can read as calling them outdated or worthless.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. It is the only answer that names a group of tribes ("Two and a half of the tribes"). Both wrong answers share one pattern: "The tribe of ___ alone." A baker can pick the odd one out without reasoning from the passage.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates Stop 1 by a wide margin: 6 multiple choice, 2 true or false and 2 fill in the blank. Cards 8, 10, 11 and 13 are four multiple choice cards in a row.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The wrong answers "question" and "rewrite" are not believable after Moses calls for obedience to the covenant. Next to them, "follow" is the only serious option, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
